scope: Remaining 36 original findings; native timeout recovery included separately

findings.title: Account-on-hold wording and browser preview disagree with native opening/increase adjustment rules

findings.fix: Purchase hold and credit limit apply to charge entries, not historical opening balances or manager corrections. Native opening_balance and adjustment posts require a nonblank reason and a currently active employee with adjust_customer_account permission, using the stored role-permission matrix. Historical entries preserve account hold, credit limit and configuration. The customer dialog explains this policy. Parent agent owns matching database.ts preview validation changes.

findings.title: New customer accounts expose ledger actions before their persisted account row exists

findings.fix: An explicit manual ledger post validates its shape, customer and adjustment actor before creating a missing account inside the same transaction. The default account is held, with zero purchase limit and zero initial balance; the ledger movement and account creation commit or roll back together. MariaDB keeps the existing dataset/report/restore guards and customer identity lock, then checks/locks the account before inserting it. Existing accounts are not upserted or reconfigured on replay. Read APIs stay side-effect-free. Checkout sale mutations retain their original account requirement and purchasing guards.

findings.title: A failed card-provider switch can disable the working provider
findings.native: No native provider-switch failure was injected and no saved provider key or configuration was changed. Confirmed-state recovery is covered by seven provider helper cases plus native source review.
findings.fix: Provider switching validates/enables the target before disabling the prior working provider. Target-save rejection never disables the prior provider and warns that the target save may be unconfirmed. If disabling the prior provider rejects, a fresh native config read determines recovery: confirmed disabled keeps the successfully enabled target; confirmed enabled restores the target's prior enabled state; a reread failure leaves the target enabled and explicitly requires reloading both settings before payment. Rollback failure also presents explicit uncertain-state recovery instructions. An initial prior-provider read failure aborts before mutation. Separate operation guards prevent overlapping switches/tests/removal. Configuration and ownership fields are retained and no secret is read or printed by tests.
findings.automatedEvidence: 7 provider helper cases: target rejection, success ordering, confirmed-enabled previous-disable rejection with target rollback, rollback rejection instructions, post-write previous-disable rejection with confirmed-disabled state, uncertain reread without rollback, and ambiguous post-write target rejection. The same file includes 2 queue cases; all 33 scoped tests passed. Artifact suite evidence: 33 tests across settingsWriteQueue, savedSettings, setupSafety, settingsHandlers, connectionPersistence and settingsBatchAudit. Source artifact: settings-followup.json.
findings.limits: Recoverable two-provider sequence, not an atomic cross-provider transaction. Before rollback, production rereads the prior provider after an ambiguous write failure; mocked tests cover confirmed-enabled, confirmed-disabled and unreadable outcomes. Native filesystem faults/failed-save branches are not a native PASS; uncertain configurations require reload/confirmation.

findings.title: Connect on an existing till reruns bootstrap data actions without an explicit reconnect-only path

findings.fix: Existing authenticated tills use explicit Save & Reconnect Only. Candidate probing occurs before replacing reactive configuration. This path bypasses all inferred repair, force push, wipe-and-pull and import branches; connection mode/credentials save in one native atomic batch. Failed candidates restore the previous state, and a post-save reconnect failure attempts to restore the previous saved configuration with explicit failure guidance if that cannot be done. First-run and confirmed pending-restore paths retain their existing identity and restore guards.
findings.automatedEvidence: Actual handleConnect fixtures: unchanged existing connection invokes no bootstrap/schema/data actions; failed probe retains prior configuration and runs no schema/data/save operations. Failed candidate, post-save failure/rollback, changed-server identity and restore branches were isolated/source tests, not native failures; absence of destructive UI is not a full tracing claim for every server operation.

findings.title: Customer-account card payments have no visible on-screen cancellation

findings.title: Failed settings saves can still appear saved
findings.native: Native feedback toggles saved confirmed off/on values and restored the original setting. Font saves also confirmed the selected value and restored Legacy. Failed saves are no longer treated as confirmed by the shared batch path.
findings.fix: Feedback, scale, printer and tax-mode settings publish only after saveSettingsBatch succeeds. Audited before-values and sanitized audit rows are prepared before commit; settings, audit records and sync outbox mutations then share the atomic local batch, avoiding a post-commit audit-read/write failure that could falsely report an already saved setting as failed. Unchanged and explicitly ignored settings omit audit rows. Failed before-reads or commit failures retain confirmed values and show an actionable error. Composite printer presets, protocols and drawer targets submit one batch. Tax mode uses this same batch, with busy guard, input lock and rollback of the draft on error.
findings.automatedEvidence: savedSettings rejected/pending persistence and coherent batch fixtures; 7 actual-production-function settingsBatchAudit VM cases covering before-read failure, shared settings/audit commit, unchanged/ignored audit omissions, commit failure without publication, preview history, secret redaction and immutable rows; maintenance-handler failure tests. All 33 scoped tests passed. Artifact suite evidence: 33 tests across settingsWriteQueue, savedSettings, setupSafety, settingsHandlers, connectionPersistence and settingsBatchAudit. Source artifact: settings-followup.json.
findings.limits: Native healthy save paths observed. Seven production-function VM tests execute batching/audit policy with mocked transaction boundaries; before-read failure, atomic commit rejection, audit sanitization and publication ordering were not native fault injected. Scale/printer/tax failure paths are not blanket native PASS.

findings.title: Item fields can save while the stock change fails
findings.native: Native Edit Item for 0EGGS (barcode 5020379111201, old-item-016480) started at stock 0, item tracking off, price 169p. With global stock tracking temporarily on, enabling item tracking and Save Item counted 0→1; UI and database confirmed stock 1/tracking on with queue 0, conflicts 0, intents 0. Reopening, counting 1→0 and disabling item tracking restored stock 0/tracking off/price 169p. Exactly two stock_counted audit rows recorded 0→1 and1→0 with the original expected-count CAS values. Global tracking was restored off.
findings.fix: Retains the existing details-then-stock persistence model but explains partial success accurately. If stock fails after details commit, editor refreshes its saved product/stock baseline before retry. If refresh fails, stale editor closes and requests reopening; no misleading generic all-or-nothing Save error. Counted stock now uses an atomic local CAS+audit batch or an online pinned MariaDB close/restore/epoch-fenced expected-stock transaction; counts cannot queue absolute stock uploads. Confirmed results survive cache/display-read failure, uncertain COMMIT explicitly prohibits repetition, and guarded cache mirrors publish stock only from an unchanged clean baseline. Generic existing-product metadata replay excludes stockLevel while preserving metadata updates and new-product opening stock.
findings.automatedEvidence: Delayed immutable item submission and duplicate guard; Details success plus stock failure refreshes stock baseline; Snapshot read failure closes stale editor Artifact suite evidence: 36 tests passed (23 catalogue/design workflow tests and 13 catalogue integrity tests). Source artifact: catalogue-design-followup.json. Final stock evidence: stock-count-review.json records 23 production-orchestration fixtures, three exact-production-SQL disposable MariaDB cases and native local batch/CAS/audit/cache guards. catalogue-stock-guard-followup.json records the generic replay metadata-preserve predicate plus an actual native MariaDB replay retaining sale-reduced stock; overlapping checks are included once in final 1,234 frontend / 251 Rust / 55 real-database totals.
findings.limits: Native healthy count/save and exact restoration passed; native stale-count races, audit failure, cache failure and uncertain COMMIT were not injected. Actual production SQL and native batch/CAS/generic-replay tests cover those boundaries separately. Details and stock remain separate commits with explicit partial-success handling. Shared counted-stock writes intentionally require online authority; legacy queued absolute counts need review/recount, not blind replay.

findings.title: Success notifications cover settings content and header actions

findings.fix: Non-blocking notifications moved from upper-right settings header/cards to a compact bottom-right stack, at most the newest two visible notices, max 22vh/180px. Click-through remains except dismiss buttons; financial/error prompts are unchanged.
findings.automatedEvidence: Source checked; no finding-specific automated execution recorded. Artifact suite evidence: 33 tests across settingsWriteQueue, savedSettings, setupSafety, settingsHandlers, connectionPersistence and settingsBatchAudit. Source artifact: settings-followup.json.
findings.limits: Observed single safe notification placement passed. Rapid two-notice stacking, every theme/layout save and every viewport are not fully native verified; blocking financial/error dialogs intentionally remain unchanged.

findings.title: Card-provider read errors are presented as Setup required
findings.native: Native provider overview showed Dojo Enabled and genuinely unconfigured SumUp Setup required after healthy reads.
findings.fix: Provider overview distinguishes Could not load settings from genuine Setup required, with Retry loading settings. Dojo and SumUp detail pages also disable destructive/save actions after an initial read failure and expose safe Retry instead of permitting defaults to overwrite unread saved configuration.
findings.automatedEvidence: Actual provider refresh fixture rejects SumUp read while returning genuinely unconfigured Dojo; independent error states are preserved. Artifact suite evidence: 33 tests across settingsWriteQueue, savedSettings, setupSafety, settingsHandlers, connectionPersistence and settingsBatchAudit. Source artifact: settings-followup.json.
findings.limits: Native healthy read states observed. Read rejection/Retry and fail-closed detail save/removal protections were tested with mocks, not by corrupting or changing provider configuration; saved keys were unchanged.

findings.title: Scale/label bounded suggestions do not explain omitted results
findings.native: Native label catalogue displayed a 76,000-item bounded result set at 100 per page; Next showed 101–200. Scale displayed its bounded 10-item result range.
findings.fix: Scale and label suggestions expose result ranges, capped total suffixes and Previous/Next. Scale pages the catalogue before hiding assigned IDs, preserving access to later unassigned matches instead of silently truncating to 60. Search scheduling invalidates stale requests immediately.
findings.automatedEvidence: Label page 2 requests offset 100 and exposes capped total; Scale page 2 requests offset 100 then filters assignments; Stale label scan result cannot add another query's item Artifact suite evidence: 36 tests passed (23 catalogue/design workflow tests and 13 catalogue integrity tests). Source artifact: catalogue-design-followup.json.
findings.limits: Native label next-page and displayed scale boundaries observed. Later unassigned scale pages, capped-total edge cases and stale searches remain isolated fixtures, not a full native catalogue traversal.

findings.title: Stock-receipt history stops at50 without receipt-line detail
findings.native: Native two-receipt stock history supported search and opened receipt detail containing three lines.
findings.fix: Stock receiving history is paged instead of silently stopping at the newest 50. It exposes receipt counts/ranges, Newer/Older controls, supplier/reference/notes filters and a read-only receipt-line details modal with quantity, unit cost, line cost, loading, empty and retry states.
findings.automatedEvidence: src/lib/stores/catalogueHistoryPersistence.test.ts executes actual SQLite queries: 65 receipts reached across deterministic non-overlapping pages, combined filters, literal/bound search safety, exact receipt lines and missing-product fallback. Stock history source-wiring assertions cover loading/zero-result paging and detail states; src/lib/stores/stockReceiptPreview.test.ts covers matching preview history behavior.
findings.limits: Native search/detail passed on the small existing history. Traversal beyond 50 receipts is actual SQLite fixture evidence, not a native >50-record scenario. Product names are current catalogue names, not historical snapshots. Final native stock count/save restoration is separately recorded under AUDIT-05.

findings.title: Suppliers lack search and paging
findings.native: Native supplier page with zero suppliers showed search and empty/paging controls without broken layout.
findings.fix: Supplier management uses the shared search strip and bounded 25-row getSuppliersPage query; company/contact/phone/email filtering and Previous/Next are available. Parent owns the SQLite query. Delayed old searches cannot replace newer results.
findings.automatedEvidence: Actual delayed supplier loader ignores stale result; Source wiring confirms bounded query and page offset Artifact suite evidence: 36 tests passed (23 catalogue/design workflow tests and 13 catalogue integrity tests). Source artifact: catalogue-design-followup.json. Actual SQLite paging, literal search, bounds and 125-supplier no-overlap traversal are covered by src/lib/stores/catalogueHistoryPersistence.test.ts.
findings.limits: Observed empty-state UI only. Populated search, large supplier paging and stale delayed searches are isolated/actual SQLite fixtures, not native large-data traversal.

implementationSummary.note: All 36 implementations are recorded: 19 explicit native scenario passes, 13 partial native observations and four automated/source-only findings. No finding-level native test is still awaiting the planned final run, but each item's untested hardware/failure matrix remains explicit. Original P1 receipt 1000085 recovery and final fixture restoration are separately verified.
